key_decisions: REPLACED the turbo LoRA rather than adding a second one. Fabio measured the larry v4_step600_ema weight we shipped in MPI-505 at close to NO-LoRA wall clock - it cut the step count and gave the time back per step. lightx2v's is a real speed-up: 105s -> 87.77s at 6 steps on the same clip.

Strength 0.75 and 6 steps are measured floors. At 1.0 the audio degrades; at 4 steps (what the weight was distilled for) audio is unusable. On H3 audio breaks BEFORE the picture does, so it must be judged on its own pass.
The two LoRAs' strengths are not comparable - lightx2v bakes alpha/r=0.125 into lora_B per its own safetensors metadata.

Deleting the old weight from R2 was safe ONLY because it never shipped (entered the tree in 0b15f342 today; `git tag --contains` empty). The MPI-470/466 rule against deleting dep entries does not apply when no release ever referenced the weight.

Wrote our own MpiVideoSamplingPreview instead of shipping KJNodes' ModelPreviewOverrideKJ. Their node base64s frames onto a private kj_preview_override WS event bound to a DOM widget - browser-only. Ours emits on the STANDARD binary preview channel plus a VHS_latentpreview marker, which the app already consumes, so it needs ZERO app-side changes.

That decision replaced an earlier plan to add a ~15-line comfyController listener plus preview_frames:1 stills. Both halves of that plan would have been deleted by the node, so the interim was skipped as MORE work, not less.

LTX needed no new node at all - only a rewire. LTX2SamplingPreviewOverride was already in the graph fed the FULL video VAE; it branches on first_stage_model being TAEHV and silently falls back to latent_rgb_factors otherwise, which is why those previews were blocky while a previewer sat right there.

Both tiny decoders live in vae/ and are NOT engineAssets, unlike the three in vae_approx/. Those are core-read and model-agnostic; these are node-read and model-owned, so a model-keyed install reaches them and GC with the last owner is correct.

MpiVideoSamplingPreview has NEVER RUN. It registers (/object_info returns its schema) and is wired correctly in both graphs, but no generation has gone through it. It also swallows preview errors by design, so its failure mode is SILENT: no frames, run completes, one line `[MpiVideoSamplingPreview] preview disabled after: ...` in the ComfyUI console. Check for that string first.

The likeliest first-run bug is the frame cursor. _temporal_ratio reads latent_format.temporal_downscale_ratio (4 for H3). Wrong there raises no error - it just makes playback the wrong speed, which is exactly the symptom Kijai's 2D taeh3 produced earlier in the session.

Use madebyollin's taeh3 (sha 4fd022bf...4c13), NOT Kijai/MiniMax-H3-TAE (sha f0f60fa0...e527, now deleted everywhere). Kijai's is 2D with no temporal layers, so it returns one image per LATENT frame and plays ~4x fast.
